messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Dealing with index out-of-bounds errors
parts:
The behavior has always bothered me. When we access things out of bounds, it doesn't actually stop the program, but instead rejects the iteration. If it's deterministic, it'll reject a bunch of times in a row and kick out.

I guess I'm thinking that size matches shouldn't throw domain errors, but something else and that we should do something more sensible with that sort of error handling.

I also believe that's the type of error handling that can be safely turned off after you've verified everything works based on shape of matrices.

Thoughts?



Daniel

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Dealing with index out-of-bounds errors
parts:
On May 29, 2014, at 12:32 PM, Daniel Lee <bea...@alum.mit.edu> wrote:

> The behavior has always bothered me. When we access things out of bounds, it doesn't actually stop the program, but instead rejects the iteration. If it's deterministic, it'll reject a bunch of times in a row and kick out.
>
> I guess I'm thinking that size matches shouldn't throw domain errors, but something else and that we should do something more sensible with that sort of error handling.

We don't have many options --- we can (a) print error messages,
(b) reject proposals, or (c) stop the whole sampler.

I wouldn't be opposed to (c) for indexing errors.
> I also believe that's the type of error handling that can be safely turned off after you've verified everything works based on shape of matrices.

This is only safe in the strict sense if all branching (including
indexing) depends only on data. I know Michael's been lobbying for
just that restriction as it removes a lot of potentially bad
non-continuous behavior.

- Bob
